questions_for_the_owner_via_the_coordina.ask: Is chapter 7 in the exam? The rules take the chapter list as a parameter (default 1 to 6); only you fix it, due 2026-10-30.
How many items, and what weight per chapter and per item type? Marks per item and the mark total. The rules only check that the answer time fits the sitting (see Q5).
Which paper size and is double-sided printing available? The measurement assumes A4 and shows sheets for both; give a page limit if there is one (the rule R17 then enforces it).

Does 'higher Bloom level' mean Apply and above (the reading used: Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create) or Analyze and above? Measured in the banks: Apply and Analyze are 718 of 1,453 items (49 percent); Analyze alone is 235 (16 percent), and chapter 6 has none.

Confirm or give the answer time per item type used by the time rule: choice 60 s, choice with code 100 s, matching 240 s, ordering 120 s, fill-in blank 45 s, number 120 s, trace 120 s, short written answer 240 s; 10 percent of the sitting is kept for reading and checking. These are working estimates, not measurements.

Do you allow the three conditional types: short written answer (reaches Evaluate; needs a marking rubric of at most 3 points), diagram labelling (needs a line drawing from the course), writing code on paper? None is used unless you enable it.
May the make-up exam repeat any midterm item? The rule warns on a repeat; say if it must be forbidden or allowed.
Answer mode: circle the letter on the item (recommended: no copying step, saves the answer-sheet pages) or a grid on the cover page? Both pass the rules.

Code width: of 427 code items in chapters 1 to 6, 302 have a line wider than 45 characters, the width that prints unwrapped in two columns. Choose: one column for code-heavy parts, shorter code lines written for the paper, or only items whose code fits. Code lines are never wrapped.

What does 'indirect question' mean for this course (for example: asks for a consequence, an exception, or the reason behind a rule instead of a definition)? No source defines it, so no rule for it is written; cross-chapter synthesis is written (a synthesis item must name two or more chapters).
